title: i18n part 3: route UI strings through tr()/tf() in batches (split of #853)
body:
## Sub-issue of #853 — Part 3: route UI strings through `tr()`/`tf()`, in batches

**Proposal, asking for a yes before any code lands.** Follow-up to the closure of #3304.

### What

Move user-visible literals to catalogue keys, one batch per PR:

1. `crates/ui` — static literals at direct egui call sites (`on_hover_text`, `label`, `button`, `checkbox`, `menu_item`), shared property vocabulary, ribbon/tree/page captions, help text, status banners. About 100 files (commits `01fb6f18`, `e2ab79fe`, `b818cf79`).
2. `crates/ui` — dynamic `format!` templates through `tf()`, so Chinese can reorder words; arguments are pre-rendered and substituted in the translated template order. About 171 files (commit `19eed997`).
3. `crates/app` — status, refusal and error text; each refusal keeps a stable name or code. About 354 files (commit `89172375`, plus `7f212d12` and `0093244c`).

Each batch opens its own PR. No batch may be combined with another.

### Why batches

The closed #3304 changed 589 files in one PR. Splitting by crate and by static/dynamic seam makes each diff reviewable and keeps a failing batch revertible without disturbing the others.

### Rules

- English is the key. A miss shows English, never a key or a blank.
- Never route G-code, CL, project files, `.mch`/`.cps`, MCP names/JSON, parsed log lines or test goldens through the catalogue.
- Structural scripts must report 0 missing keys before a batch is proposed.
- Tests and AccessKit checks match by stable ids, not English labels.

### Acceptance

- App fully in Chinese for the batch's surface, with English fallback for any untranslated key.
- Posted output byte-identical in every language.
- `scripts/i18n/check.py` exits 0.

### Depends on

Part 1 and Part 2. Each batch is independent of the later batches.
